title: learn v0.2: Interactive Content Framework (Preact + components)
description:
Add Preact + htm + a fixed component library to the frontend. No build step. Lessons become structured documents with mixed markdown blocks and component specs.

## Why
Plain markdown lessons are dull. Real learning needs interactive widgets — runnable code, animated diagrams, step-throughs, embedded quizzes.

## Decision
Preact (~3kb) + htm (tagged template literals, JSX-like, no build step) + marked (already loaded) + mermaid (added). Loaded from CDN. Total weight ~80kb gzipped.

## Components in the initial library
- Callout (info / warning / insight / takeaway)
- CodeRunner (sandboxed iframe, JS)
- Mermaid (text-to-SVG)
- SvgFigure (raw SVG, sanitised)
- StepThrough (animated walkthrough with Next button)
- FlashcardDeck (inline flashcards)
- ConceptMap (small interactive graph)
- Highlight (wraps content; click reveals Explain/Example/Why actions)

## Lesson document format
JSON: { blocks: [{type:'markdown', content}, {type:'component', kind, props}] }
Lesson generator agent updated to emit this. Backwards-compat: string-only lessons become a single markdown block.

## Renderer
Preact <LessonRenderer> walks blocks, dispatches to component library.

## Safety
Code runs in sandboxed iframe (no network, no parent DOM). SVG sanitised. Component props validated server-side before render.

## Acceptance
- Existing v0.1 lessons render unchanged (backwards compat)
- New lessons can include all 8 component types
- Page weight under 150kb gzipped on first load
- No build step — viewable straight from a static HTML file

title: learn v0.2: Dashboard & Discovery (surfaces)
description:
The new home page. Surfaces what the patrol found, plus jump-back-in / daily quiz / daily flashcards / insights feed / cross-course connections / graph snapshot.

## Why
v0.1's home is a flat course list. The dashboard should be a personalised, graph-driven surface where the system shows you what matters now.

## Scope
- /api/dashboard endpoint (composed bundle of all sections)
- New flashcards table + flashcard-generator agent (Haiku)
- "Daily" semantics — fresh-on-demand, not strict 24h
- Adaptive quiz selection across all courses (weighted by blast radius + decay)
- Dashboard view in frontend, replaces Courses as the home tab
- Flashcard flip-card UI; "knew it" / "didn't know it" feeds back to the graph via record_understanding/record_confusion
- Insights feed: recent undismissed insights, dismiss + viewed states

## Cards on the dashboard
1. Jump back in (most recent quiz_attempt or chat_message)
2. Daily quiz (one adaptive question)
3. Flashcards for review (decay candidates)
4. Insights feed (from patrol)
5. Cross-course connections
6. Graph snapshot (concept count, recent growth)

nmemo-umy (Phase 1 patrol layer)

title: learn v0.2: Background Patrol Layer (foundation)
description:
Cron-driven analysis layer for the learn platform. Reads Graph S/C and writes insights to a feed that the dashboard consumes.

## Why
Nothing in v0.1 runs unless the user clicks. The system can't surface anything proactively without a process that thinks while the user is away.

## Scope
- New SQLite tables: insights, patrol_runs
- Cron service in learn/src/index.ts (default 30min interval, env-configurable, off in dev)
- Patrol agent: Sonnet, MCP-driven, bounded (max 5 insights / 12 turns per run)
- New MCP tools: get_decay_candidates, find_cross_course_overlaps, find_dense_clusters, write_insight
- Mutex on in-flight patrols
- Manual trigger endpoint /api/patrol/run-now for testing
- Observability endpoint /api/patrol/runs

## Insight types (emergent vocabulary, not fixed enum)
- decay_warning, cross_course_link, prerequisite_gap, pattern_emerging, synthesis_candidate, contradiction_detected

## Acceptance
- Patrol runs on cron, writes insights, never duplicates on (type, related_entity_ids)
- Manual /api/patrol/run-now works and returns a run_id
- /api/patrol/runs shows last N runs with stats (insights_written, mcp_calls, duration_ms)
- Idempotent: re-running same patrol against unchanged graph produces no new insights
- All inserts/updates traceable via patrol_runs.id reference

title: HARDEN-P1: Evolve Phase 1 test fixtures via test-harden skill BEFORE implementation

Implementation code in Phase 1 must pass tests written against these hardened fixtures, not the scaffolds. Success criteria:
1. At least 3 hardened fixtures per L1 scenario in Phase 1 (simple-mutations, concurrent-races, actor-escalation, cascade-writes, invalid-actors)

This task does NOT require Phase 1 code to exist. The skill's Data Evolver subagent can evolve fixtures without seeing code (by design — that's the anti-test-fitting property). It can't run vitest end-to-end, but it can still produce richer fixtures.

title: Cluster bridging — reconciliation agent connects disconnected narrative threads
description:
## Context

The extraction agent produces two disconnected clusters from Frankenstein:
- **Walton cluster** (95 nodes): R. Walton, Margaret, the stranger, Archangel, etc. — richly connected
- **Frankenstein cluster** (~10 nodes): Victor Frankenstein, Beaufort, Caroline, Alphonse, Geneva, Lucerne — internally connected but isolated

The bridge should be: the stranger = Victor Frankenstein (same person, different narrative voice). The extraction agent correctly identifies both entities but can't make the connection because:
- The stranger is described in 3rd person by Walton (chunks 1-9)
- Victor narrates in 1st person (chunk 10+)
- The identity link only becomes visible after BOTH entities exist

The extraction agent's reports contain the evidence:
- Stranger's summary: "agreed to share his life story", "storyteller who will reveal his tale"
- Victor's aliases: "I (narrator of Chapter 1, Victor's autobiography)"
- Chunk 10 report: "I / my → Victor Frankenstein (narrator recounting family history)"

## What the reconciliation agent does

Runs after extraction, reads:
1. Entity summaries — look for narrative transition indicators
2. Entity aliases — look for shared/overlapping references (both have "I" as alias)
3. Merge candidates from graph meta
4. Extraction reports (FACTS SKIPPED, DIFFICULTIES sections)

Actions:
- **same_as link**: the stranger ↔ Victor Frankenstein (preserves both entities, different narrative meaning)
- **merge**: R. Walton = Robert Walton (same entity, same meaning — if duplicates exist)
- **alias**: Margaret = Mrs. Saville (add alias, keep canonical)
- **bridge facts**: create facts that connect clusters (e.g., "the stranger child_of Alphonse" if evidence supports it)

Key constraint: facts on both entities MUST be preserved when creating same_as links. A same_as link doesn't merge — it connects while keeping both nodes and their facts intact.

## Evidence the agent has available

- Entity summaries describing narrative roles and transitions
- Self-describing aliases with narrator context
- Source material searchable via Qdrant
- Graph structure (shared patterns, structural similarity)
- Extraction reports noting skipped facts and difficulties
- merge_candidates table with three-signal scores

## Depends on
- Entity summaries (implemented)
- Self-describing aliases (implemented)
- Graph meta merge candidates (implemented)
- Extraction agent reports (implemented — logged, could be stored)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reconciliation agent endpoint with system prompt
- [ ] Runs after extraction when disconnected clusters or unconfirmed aliases are detected
- [ ] Creates same_as links for identity matches with different narrative meaning
- [ ] Executes merges for clear duplicates via merge_entities() SQL function
- [ ] Creates bridge facts when evidence supports cross-cluster relationships
- [ ] Records reasoning in merge_candidates.resolution_reasoning
- [ ] Facts preserved on both sides of same_as links
- [ ] Visible in viz — same_as links shown as a distinct edge type

title: learn v0.2: Cross-Course Intelligence (synthesis)
description:
Same-as detection across courses + connection-finder + article generator. The graph genuinely paying off pedagogically.

## Why
The user takes a JS course, then a Rust course. Closures appear in both. The system already detects entity overlap via Nmemo's same_as_links. Pedagogically: this is a teaching opportunity, not a data-cleanup problem. We surface the connection.

## Scope
- Connection-finder agent runs on patrol (Phase 1 dependency): walks same_as_links and merge_candidates between concept entities in different courses; for non-trivial overlaps writes cross_course_link insights
- Article generator agent: when patrol detects a dense cluster (5+ concepts the learner has touched recently across multiple courses), generates a synthesis article. Stored as a special "synthesis" entity; surfaced on the dashboard
- Bridge UI element: at the top of any section, show "you've seen this before in [Course X]" link if a cross-course link exists for that concept
- Cross-course connections card on the dashboard

## Acceptance
- Two courses sharing a concept produce a cross_course_link insight on the next patrol
- Article generator produces a coherent synthesis when given a 5+ concept cluster
- Dashboard surfaces the connection card
- Section view shows the "seen before" bridge link when applicable

## Depends on
nmemo-umy (Phase 1 patrol)

title: learn v0.2: Lesson Evolution (overlays, versioning, notes, highlights)
description:
Per-learner lesson overlays so chat-driven edits don't mutate canonical course content. Versioned. Highlight + popover annotations. Notes feature with selective promotion to graph.

## Why
Canonical course content shouldn't change for everyone when one learner asks for a clarification. AI edits sometimes make things worse — we need a way back. Notes deserve to feed the graph but only when the learner says so.

## Scope
- New tables: lesson_overlays(learner_id, section_id, blocks JSON, version, created_at), notes(id, learner_id, section_id, anchor_text, content_md, promoted_to_graph)
- Chat MCP tool: edit_lesson_section(section_id, edit_op) — writes to overlay only, never canonical
- Edit ops: insert_block, replace_block, append_clarification, add_example
- Versioning UI: view history per section, revert to version N
- Highlight selection in frontend → action menu (Explain / Example / Why / Take a note)
- Lightweight on-demand explainer agent for popovers (Haiku, ~5s)
- Notes UI: per-section note panel
- "Promote note to graph" button calls record_understanding or record_confusion

## Acceptance
- Editing a lesson via chat updates only the current learner's overlay
- Reverting brings back exact prior version
- Highlights persist (stored as ranges in notes table or annotations table)
- Notes are private by default; only promoted ones become graph facts
- Multi-learner safe: two learners taking the same course see different overlays

nmemo-8z5 (Phase 3 component framework), nmemo (Phase 4 component generation, but soft)

title: learn v0.2: Dynamic Component Generation (chat-orchestrated)
description:
Component-generator agent orchestrated by the chat tutor. The chat can produce live, contextual interactive components — Mermaid diagrams, SVG figures, code examples, step-through animations — inline in its responses.

## Why
The diagnostic moment ("you don't get reverse-in-place") deserves a SHOW, not a TELL. A 6-step animated walkthrough beats a paragraph every time.

## Scope
- New component-generator agent (Sonnet, bounded — one component per chat turn unless explicitly more requested)
- New MCP tool: generate_component(kind, context)
- Chat tutor's response becomes a structured document (same blocks format as lessons)
- Chat UI renders components inline (live Mermaid, runnable code, animations)
- "Save to lesson" button promotes a generated component to the per-learner lesson overlay (depends on Phase 5)

## Pattern
1. User: "I don't get how reverse-in-place works"
2. Chat tutor MCP loop:
   a. get_learner_understanding("reverse linked list") — confirms weak
   b. generate_component({kind: 'StepThrough', ...}) — produces 6-step walkthrough
   c. Returns structured doc: markdown + component
3. UI renders the chat message including the live component

title: Graph agent invocation fails: Claude CLI exits rc=1 — gates 3 causal integration tests + live ingest
description:
## Symptom

`Error: Graph agent failed (500): Claude CLI failed (rc=1)` thrown at
`platform/src/services/causal-agent.ts:2177` from `invokeGraphAgent`.

The `500` originates from the Python ML service `${ML_SERVICES_URL}/graph-agent`
endpoint (`ml-services/app/graph_agent.py`), which spawns a `claude -p ...`
subprocess with the graph_agent MCP config. The subprocess exits non-zero and
the ML service surfaces "Claude CLI failed (rc=1)" in the 500 body, which the
platform then re-throws verbatim.

stderr from the subprocess is not currently captured/forwarded to the platform
caller — that's part of why this is opaque.

## Reproducer

Against a running stack (`make up` + `make ml`):

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/ingest/queue \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"<any non-trivial paragraph>", "source":"manual"}'
```

Or hit the ML endpoint directly to bypass the platform:

```bash
curl -X POST "${ML_SERVICES_URL}/graph-agent" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"source_text":"...", "memory_id":"<uuid>", "mcp_config_path":"<path>", "source_name":"manual"}'
```

## Gated integration tests

All in `platform/src/test/harness/`:

- `causal-integration.test.ts` — `B06 Integration: Causal MCP + Claude Code > Claude Code creates causal edge from explicit causal language` (line 103). Line 85 (`tools exposed`) does not invoke the CLI.
- `causal-chains.test.ts` — `B09: Multi-input causal chains > 3 sequential ingests produce causal chain spanning multiple memories` (line 45) and `> all edges created during this test have valid quality` (line 80). Both call ingest end-to-end.
- `causal-trigger.test.ts` — the four `it('agent DOES run …')` cases at lines 88, 102, 115, 138. The `does NOT run` and pure trigger-detection cases are unaffected.

These three failed in the full `pnpm test` run on `feat/reasoning-agent` HEAD
(`8082c87`, Phase 6 G7). The 332 deterministic harness tests + 63
pattern-suite tests are all green; the failure is isolated to the live-CLI
path.

## Scope / blame

Not introduced by Phase 6 (`nmemo-d9v`). Phase 6 didn't touch `graph_agent`,
its prompt, or the CLI invocation path. Pre-existing on `feat/reasoning-agent`
and likely on `feat/cognitive-platform-v1` baseline. The Phase 6 work simply
made the failure visible by running a complete `pnpm test`.
design: Suspected causes (to investigate, in rough likelihood order): (1) Claude CLI auth state — token expiry, missing login, or env-var unset in the ML service process tree. (2) MCP config path resolution — graph_agent MCP config not found or unparseable from inside the spawned subprocess. (3) Model unavailability — default model retired/renamed in CLI config. (4) Prompt size or stdin pipe handling on Windows — the `claude -p` invocation may be choking on large source_text payloads or CRLF stdio. (5) Working directory / cwd assumption — subprocess spawned from ml-services dir but expects platform cwd. Investigation plan: (a) capture the rc=1 subprocess stderr + stdout in `ml-services/app/graph_agent.py` and forward in the 500 body so future failures are diagnosable; (b) add a one-shot smoke test that runs `claude -p "echo hi"` with the graph_agent MCP config and asserts rc=0; (c) once root cause known, fix and re-enable the 3 integration tests under their original `it()` blocks (no skips).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Capture and forward subprocess stderr+stdout in ml-services/app/graph_agent.py so the platform error message contains actionable diagnostic detail rather than just "rc=1". AC2: All three integration tests pass without skips on a clean `pnpm test` run: causal-integration.test.ts B06 (line 103), causal-chains.test.ts B09 (lines 45 + 80), causal-trigger.test.ts B07 four `agent DOES run` cases (lines 88, 102, 115, 138). AC3: `POST /ingest/queue` end-to-end against a clean MISRA corpus (re-ingested via the viz Ingest panel) completes without surfacing "Graph agent failed (500): Claude CLI failed (rc=1)". AC4: A regression smoke test exists that asserts `claude -p` runs successfully with the graph_agent MCP config (so future env drift is caught earlier than the integration suite).
notes: Surfaced 2026-04-28 during the post-Phase-6 full pnpm test run on feat/reasoning-agent HEAD 8082c87. The test-harden loop should pick this up as a real failure (not a flake) once it scopes phase6/integration scenarios. Filed under nmemo-klv per resume-prompt dialogue 2026-04-29 — framed as "integration suite is gated and the test-harden loop should pick it up". Reference: src/services/causal-agent.ts:2161-2181 (invokeGraphAgent).

title: Optimise applyConfidenceDecay: 100-edge cycle exceeds 200ms AC target
description:
Surfaced by klv.2 fixture-driven benchmark on phase2-lifecycle/fixtures/decay-battlefield.sql (100 edges, 60 decay-eligible). Measured: p50=286ms, p95=303ms on local docker postgres. AC target from klv.2: <200ms / 100 edges. Gap: ~100ms.

Root cause: applyConfidenceDecay (src/services/causal.ts:597) runs a per-row serial loop where each iteration opens a fresh transaction, runs SELECT FOR UPDATE, UPDATE, and INSERT INTO causal_edge_history. With 60 decay-eligible rows that's 60 transactions × ~5ms each.

Optimisation paths to evaluate:
1. Single UPDATE ... RETURNING wrapped in CTE to compute new strength + conditionally expire, then bulk-insert audit rows in one statement.
2. Keep per-row transaction but pipeline the SELECT FOR UPDATE + UPDATE into one statement.
3. Drop the second SELECT FOR UPDATE pass entirely if the candidate query already covers the qualifier (the FOR UPDATE re-check exists to handle concurrent corroboration races — verify this is still needed once batched).

Acceptance: applyConfidenceDecay p95 < 200ms across 5 trials of decay-battlefield.sql, with all existing edge-lifecycle.test.ts assertions still green (especially the per-row audit assertions and the corroborated-skip / floor-skip / non-llm-skip cohorts).
close_reason: Replaced per-row tx loop with single-CTE batched UPDATE + INSERT…RETURNING. Decay cycle for 100 edges: p95 303ms → 6.5ms (50× speedup, AC target <200ms now met with 30× headroom). All 46 edge-lifecycle tests pass plus 65/65 across audit-trail + source-refs-index. Test threshold tightened to <50ms. Concurrency model preserved — UPDATE WHERE qualifier re-evaluates against committed state, same protection against corroboration races. See updated 2026-04-27-decay-battlefield.md for before/after.

title: [code-bug] audit.ts: case-variant actor reaches DB CHECK instead of service-layer rejection
description:
`recordFactChange` (and presumably `recordEdgeChange`) in platform/src/services/audit.ts does not validate the `actor` parameter against the allowed canonical values before issuing the raw INSERT into `public.fact_history`. A case-variant value (e.g. "Reasoning_Agent") therefore surfaces as a Postgres SQLSTATE 23514 check-constraint violation on `valid_fact_actor` rather than a friendly service-layer `Error('actor must be one of …')`. TypeScript's `Actor` union type does not protect against runtime strings arriving from MCP/JSON callers, so an explicit case-sensitive allow-list check is needed at the top of each mutation function.

Affected: platform/src/services/audit.ts:142, function recordFactChange (and likely recordEdgeChange around line 152)
Discovered by: test-harden skill, scenario phase1/simple-mutations, run 2026-04-27

## Symptom
Assertion failure in audit-trail.test.ts:482 — "expected service-layer rejection, got 23514 from DB". Expected error matching /actor must be one of/ but received: `new row for relation "fact_history" violates check constraint "valid_fact_actor"`.

## Hypothesis
The function jumps straight from the existing `reasoning` non-empty check to the raw `INSERT` SQL without comparing `params.actor` to the canonical lowercase actor values the DB CHECK enforces. The DB constraint is doing the validation work the service layer was supposed to do, producing an opaque user-facing error and breaking the phase-1 acceptance criterion that mutation functions enforce actor validity.

## Suggested direction
Add a case-sensitive allow-list check at the top of `recordFactChange` (and `recordEdgeChange`) that throws a service-level Error with a message including "actor must be one of" plus the allowed values when `params.actor` is not in the canonical set. Share the allowed-values list between the migration's CHECK definition and the service module so the two layers cannot drift. No DB-level changes required — the CHECK should remain as the last line of defence.

## Agent feedback (if applicable)
N/A — agent reasoning reports were not attached to this run.

title: Reconciliation Agent — same_as links from extraction reports
description:
## Context

The extraction agent already identifies cross-entity references in its reports but doesn't act on them:
- Chunk 6: "the stranger / he / him → Unnamed rescued person"
- Chunk 10: "I / my → The narrator (Victor Frankenstein, but unnamed in this excerpt)"
- Chunk 10: "my father → The narrator's father (unnamed proper noun)"

The agent does the hard reasoning but the rules prevent it from creating entities for generic references. A reconciliation agent should read these reports and create same_as links + missing entities.

## Design

Specialised agent that runs after extraction, reads:
1. The extraction agent's PHASE 6 reports (stored or logged)
2. The merge_candidates table from graph meta
3. The entity_meta statistics

Actions it can take:
- Create same_as links (the stranger ↔ Victor Frankenstein)
- Execute merges via merge_entities() SQL function (R. Walton = Robert Walton)
- Create alias links (Margaret = Mrs. Saville)
- Mark entities as distinct (confirm they are NOT the same)
- Create bridge entities (Victor Frankenstein) that connect disconnected clusters
- Terminate aged orphans that can't be connected

Uses the same unified graph MCP server — all tools available.

## Depends on
- Graph meta Phase 2 (graph_stats table for adaptive weighting)
- Extraction agent reports being stored (currently just logged)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reconciliation agent endpoint created
- [ ] System prompt with merge/link/alias decision framework
- [ ] Reads extraction reports + merge candidates + entity meta
- [ ] Creates same_as links for identity matches with different narrative meaning
- [ ] Executes merges for clear duplicates
- [ ] Records reasoning in merge_candidates.resolution_reasoning
- [ ] Triggered after extraction when candidates exist above threshold

title: Orphan Entity Detector — Aged orphan detection + resolution agent
description:
## Context

The extraction pipeline produces orphan entities — entities that get extracted and linked to source memories but never gain any facts (relationships). In the Frankenstein test, 12/21 entities had mentions but zero facts. These orphans clutter the graph and confuse the visualization.

## Design: Aged Orphan Detection + Resolution

### Detection (graph meta layer)

Add an orphan detector to the graph meta computation:
- Query: `entity_meta WHERE fact_count = 0 AND mention_count > 0 AND first_mentioned_at < NOW() - threshold`
- Threshold: configurable, default = after 3 chunks have been processed since the entity was created
- Don't flag orphans immediately — they might get facts from the next chunk
- Track orphan age in entity_meta or a new field

### Resolution (agent-based)

When aged orphans are detected, run a targeted "social services" agent:
1. For each orphan: read its source mentions and context
2. Search the graph for entities it might relate to
3. Try to find at least one relationship from the source text
4. If a relationship is found: create the fact (orphan becomes a citizen)
5. If no relationship can be found after investigation: mark for termination

### Termination

Entities that can't be connected after agent review:
- Remove from entities table (cascade deletes memory_entities links)
- Record in entity_merges as merge_method='orphan_cleanup' for audit trail
- Log what was removed and why

### Trigger

Runs after the graph meta update in the pipeline, only when orphans exist above the age threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Orphan detection query added to graph-meta.ts
- [ ] Orphan age threshold configurable
- [ ] Resolution agent endpoint created (or reuse graph agent with orphan-specific prompt)
- [ ] Orphans either gain facts or get terminated
- [ ] Audit trail for terminated entities
- [ ] Viz shows orphan candidates (similar to merge candidates)

title: Serial baseline: Frankenstein 10-chunk sequential ingestion test
description:
## Context

The current Frankenstein regression test ingests 10 chunks in parallel via `Promise.allSettled()`. This loses temporal ordering and produces non-deterministic graphs (see `docs/architecture/truth-graph/05-temporal-pipeline-redesign.md`).

Before redesigning the pipeline, we need a serial baseline that establishes the "correct" graph when chunks are processed in document order.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New test file** `platform/src/test/harness/frankenstein-serial.test.ts` that:
   - Loads the same 10 Frankenstein chunks in document order
   - Ingests them **sequentially** (for-loop with await, NOT Promise.allSettled)
   - Passes the same quality targets as the parallel test (0 dupes, <7% mismatch, 0 duplicate facts)

2. **Capture graph snapshot** after serial ingestion:
   - Entity count + canonical names + types
   - Fact count + full triples (subject, predicate, object, confidence)
   - Causal events created (count, transition types)
   - Any errors/warnings in stderr

3. **Compare against parallel test** — document the divergence:
   - Entity count difference
   - Fact count difference (which facts are missing/extra?)
   - Causal event count difference
   - Are the same entity names resolved? Same predicates?

4. **No FK violations** — serial ingestion should produce zero `causal_events_fact_id_fkey` errors since there's no parallel mutation

5. **Output comparison** logged to stdout at test end (like the existing regression results block)

## Notes

- This test will be slower than the parallel version (sequential ML calls). Increase timeout to 600s.
- Don't change the parallel test — keep both. The parallel test documents current behavior, serial test documents correct behavior.
- The delta between them quantifies exactly what the temporal pipeline redesign needs to fix.

title: Session report passing — previous agent report as context for next session
description:
## Context

Each extraction agent session produces a structured PHASE 6 REPORT with:
- Entities found, pronouns resolved, facts created/skipped
- Difficulties and observations  
- Aliases created (including unconfirmed)

Currently this report is logged but not passed to the next agent session. The next session starts fresh with only graph state (facts, summaries, aliases) — it doesn't know what the previous session struggled with or concluded.

## Proposal

Pass the previous session's report (or a condensed version) as additional context to the next agent session. This gives the agent continuity:
- "Previous session noted: the stranger may transition to first-person narrator"
- "Previous session could not resolve: 'my father' — no proper noun available"
- "Previous session created unconfirmed alias: stranger → Victor Frankenstein"

## Considerations

- This is injected context, which we want to minimise. But it's temporary — once the graph carries the information properly (via summaries, aliases, facts), the report context becomes redundant.
- Could store reports in a table keyed by memory_id, or just pass the last N reports as a sliding window.
- Should be optional/configurable — the agent should work without it, this just accelerates convergence.
- May not be needed if aliases + summaries carry enough information.

## Status: Research — evaluate after aliases + summaries are tested
